newsitem.title: USA: Toro says "cautious" about spring season.
newsitem.headline: Toro says "cautious" about spring season.

text.p: Toro Co, which makes and sells outdoor maintenance and beautification products, said Thursday it is cautious about the spring season.

"Our product lines are strong and we continue to invest in research and development for our future. However, we are cautious about the spring season given the conservative buying mood that exists across many markets due to weather and generally high industry inventory levels," Kendrick Melrose, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Earlier, Toro reported earnings for the first quarter ended January 31 of $0.20 a share, down from $0.67 a share. Quarterly sales fell to $209.0 million from $211.5 million a year earlier.
Toro said results met its revised expectations.
The company also said that the integration of the newly acquired James Hardie Irrigation Group was on schedule.
"While we are disappointed in our earnings level compared to last year, the quarter's performance was satisfactory given the unusual aspects of the period," Melrose said.
As reported last month, several factors contributed to lower profits compared with last year, including the James Hardie Irrigation acquisition, Toro said.

"Also, several of our new businesses continued to show positive sales results during the quarter but have not reached profitable levels," Melrose said. "Finally, a shift in shipping patterns, our continued field inventory management, competitive intensity and several softening core markets resulted in lower sales in the quarter."
Sales of consumer business products for the quarter decreased by 18.5 percent.
Sales of walk power mowers and riding products were lower than last year at this time partly because Toro is shipping product closer to consumer demand for the spring season.

Snowthrower sales increased in the quarter, and the overall season was successful, Toro said. However, a lack of significant snow in the East caused higher retail inventories at quarter-end. Sales of electric handheld products rose slightly.

Commercial equipment sales were flat for the quarter reflecting continued field inventory management. Sales of equipment to other commercial customers and landscape contractors were also lower than last year.

Sales of irrigation products increased 55.1 percent due primarily to the addition of James Hardie Irrigation, Toro said. Core irrigation product sales were down for the quarter due to wet weather conditions and field inventory adjustments.

Toro said its international sales rose 37.1 percent, due in part ot the addition of Hardie sales. Toro's core international business also increased, led by sales of commercial equipment products to golf courses, particularly in the Pacific Rim, and sales of consumer products to Canada and Australia.
